from pathlib import Path
import json
from fractions import Fraction as F
root=Path('data/generated/trained_prediction_sampling/review_v2_B')
source='\\n'.join(Path('docs/global_nonlinear.md').read_text().splitlines()[5267:11436])
start=source.index('"'```python'"\\nfrom fractions import Fraction as F\\nN = 1000')+len('"'```python'"\\n')
end=source.index('\\n"'```'"',start)
(root/'reference_certificate.py').write_text(source[start:end]+'\\n')
# Independent exact check of the cutoff product identity for nontrivial values.
c=[F(2,7),F(1,3),F(3,5),F(5,6)]
v=[F(3,4),F(-2,5),F(7,9),F(-5,11)]
direct=c[3]*v[3]-c[1]*v[1]-c[2]*v[2]+c[0]*v[0]
rhs=c[3]*(v[3]-v[1]-v[2]+v[0])+(c[3]-c[1])*(v[1]-v[0])+(c[3]-c[2])*(v[2]-v[0])+(c[3]-c[1]-c[2]+c[0])*v[0]
assert direct==rhs
# Gaussian zero-rank boundary: E X"'^4=3t''^2 for C(t)=t, t>=0.
# The covariance second derivative formula gives (1/4)*d_x''^4 x''^4=6 at t=0.
assert F(1,4)*24==6
# Exact ordinary Frobenius normalization for a rank at n=3.
a=[F(1),F(-2),F(3)]; b=[F(2),F(4),F(-1)]; n=3
lhs=sum((x*y/n)**2 for x in a for y in b)
rhs=sum(x*x for x in a)/n*sum(y*y for y in b)/n
assert lhs==rhs
r={'"'status':'PASS','cutoff_product_identity':str(direct),'rank_zero_gaussian_second_derivative':6,'finite_rank_Frobenius_identity':str(lhs),'limitation':'Supplemental identity checks only; mathematical arguments establish the estimates and asymptotic conclusions.'}
